questions.q: What does the Apex expression `10 / 3` evaluate to, and why?
options: 3.33, because Apex always rounds division results to two decimal places
3, because dividing two Integer values performs integer division, which truncates anything after the decimal point rather than rounding
An error, because Apex cannot divide two Integers
10, because the division operator is ignored for whole numbers
questions.explain: The lesson explains that dividing two Integer values truncates the decimal portion entirely (not rounds), so 10 / 3 evaluates to 3; getting 3.333... requires at least one operand to be a Double or Decimal.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the practical difference between `=` and `==` in Apex?
options: They are interchangeable and always produce the same result
`=` is the assignment operator that stores a value into a variable; `==` is the equality comparison operator that checks whether two values are equal and produces a Boolean
`=` is only used for Strings, and `==` is only used for numbers
`==` assigns a value, and `=` compares two values
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes assignment (storing a value, `=`) from equality comparison (checking equality and producing a Boolean, `==`), and flags confusing the two as one of the most common beginner mistakes across languages.

questions.q: What does the logical AND operator (`&&`) require, per this lesson's example `cartHasItems && paymentValid`?
options: At least one of the two Booleans must be true
Neither Boolean may be true
Both Booleans must be true for the overall expression to be true
The two Booleans must have different values from each other
questions.explain: The lesson defines && as requiring both sides to be true, contrasting it with || (at least one side true) and ! (flips a single Boolean's value).

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend using parentheses even when a programmer has memorized operator precedence rules?
options: Because Apex requires parentheses around every single expression with no exceptions
Because parentheses make code run measurably faster
Because parentheses cost nothing and remove all ambiguity, both for the compiler and for the next person reading the code
Because operator precedence does not actually exist in Apex
questions.explain: The lesson notes that while Apex does follow standard precedence rules (like multiplication before addition), relying on memorized rules is a habit worth breaking since explicit parentheses remove ambiguity for both the compiler and human readers, at no cost.

questions.q: What is the difference between an expression and a statement, as this lesson defines them?
options: An expression is any piece of code that evaluates to a single value; a statement is a complete instruction, often built from one or more expressions, that does something with that value
A statement always contains exactly one operator, while an expression can contain any number
Expressions can only appear inside loops, while statements can appear anywhere
There is no meaningful difference between the two terms
questions.explain: The lesson gives `5 + 3` as an expression (evaluates to 8) and `Integer total = 5 + 3;` as a statement (takes that expression's value and assigns it), illustrating that statements are complete instructions built from expressions.
